A rotating phasor: its projection on the y axis is A sin(wt)

Animation of a rotating phasor. On the left, an arrow (the phasor) of length A rotates counter-clockwise about the origin, its tip tracing a circle; the angle omega t from the x axis is marked. On the right, the height of the tip, A sin(omega t), is plotted against time and traced out as the phasor turns: a horizontal line carries the tip's height across to the curve and a vertical bar from the time axis marks the current value. The curve is a sine wave.
